proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Chemistry Plan: benzylamine (Stream B) must not contact DPDTC before thioester formation is complete. Stage 1 effluent (thioester intermediate + residual DMAP + 2-pyridinethiol byproduct in 2-MeTHF) is mixed with Stream B at a T-mixer placed downstream of Reactor 1 and upstream of Reactor 2. A PEEK or ETFE T-mixer (P-713 or P-632) is used. This replicates the batch sequential addition (cool, open, add benzylamine, reseal, reheat) in a continuous connected process without a physical cooling step.

Prepare Stream B containing benzylamine (1.05 equiv relative to substrate, neat or concentrated in 2-MeTHF) in 2-MeTHF (2-methyltetrahydrofuran) at 2.1 M; concentration basis: chemistry_plan.
Install Stage 1 reactor coil_row12 (10 mL, 2.4 mm ID, ETFE) at 95 deg C.
Install Stage 2 reactor coil_row11 (5 mL, 2.4 mm ID, ETFE) at 95 deg C.
Install assigned feeds A:pump_e_series_blue, B:pump_e_series_blue.
Set the outlet BPR to 7 bar gauge and start liquid feeds at final outlet flow 0.35 mL/min.

proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Chemistry Plan: benzylamine (Stream B) must not contact DPDTC before thioester formation is complete. Stage 1 effluent (thioester intermediate + residual DMAP + 2-pyridinethiol byproduct in 2-MeTHF) is mixed with Stream B at a T-mixer placed downstream of Reactor 1 and upstream of Reactor 2. Prepare Stream B containing benzylamine (1.05 equiv relative to substrate, neat or concentrated in 2-MeTHF) in 2-MeTHF (2-methyltetrahydrofuran) at 2.1 M; concentration basis: chemistry_plan.
Install Stage 1 reactor coil_row3 (2 mL, 1 mm ID, PFA) at 95 deg C.
Install Stage 2 reactor coil_row11 (5 mL, 2.4 mm ID, ETFE) at 95 deg C.
Install assigned feeds A:pump_e_series_blue, B:pump_e_series_blue.
Set the outlet BPR to 7 bar gauge and start liquid feeds at final outlet flow 0.1 mL/min.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates.

### Design objective
Develop a safe, reproducible, and inventory-compatible two-stage telescoped flow process that maximizes the final amide yield while avoiding unnecessarily long residence times. Design the two stages as one connected process, because Stage 1 determines the composition entering Stage 2.

computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates.

computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

DrChemistry.justification: Both stages below batch anchor (τ1=17.9 min, τ2=14.3 min; ratios 0.60/0.48). Provides the shortest-time exploratory point. Uses two ETFE 5 mL coils at highest throughput (0.14 mmol/min). Adequate as a sub-batch baseline screening point; Stage 1 thioester formation and Stage 2 aminolysis may both be incomplete at these holds.
uncertainties: Stage 1 thioester conversion unknown at 17.9 min; sub-batch hold may leave unreacted acid.
Stage 2 aminolysis at 14.3 min may be insufficient; untested.
DPDTC solubility in 2-MeTHF at 0.525 M unconfirmed.
T-mixer for Stage 2 Stream B introduction not enumerated in candidate equipment list.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 sub-batch (τ1=16.7 min, ratio 0.56) in compact 2 mL PFA coil; Stage 2 above batch anchor (τ2=33.3 min, ratio 1.11) in ETFE 5 mL coil. This asymmetry (shorter thioester formation, longer aminolysis) matches the chemist hypothesis that Stage 2 may need adequate exposure. Differentiates Stage 1 speed from Stage 2 completeness. Throughput 0.06 mmol/min.
uncertainties: Stage 1 thioester completeness at 16.7 min is unknown; incomplete Stage 1 will reduce Stage 2 yield.
Whether extra Stage 2 time compensates incomplete Stage 1 is untested.
Stream B at 0.03 mL/min is near E-series minimum; pulsation may affect reproducibility.
DPDTC solubility unconfirmed.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 above batch anchor (τ1=35.7 min, ratio 1.19) in ETFE 10 mL coil; Stage 2 sub-batch (τ2=14.3 min, ratio 0.48) in ETFE 5 mL coil. Tests whether complete thioester formation in Stage 1 compensates short Stage 2. Complementary asymmetry to candidate 2. Throughput 0.14 mmol/min.
uncertainties: Stage 2 aminolysis at 14.3 min may be insufficient for full amide yield; unknown.
Whether Stage 1 is complete at 35.7 min is uncharacterized.
T-mixer for Stream B introduction not enumerated.

DrChemistry.justification: Both stages near batch anchor (τ1=31.3 min ratio 1.04, τ2=25.0 min ratio 0.83); closest symmetric match to batch 30/30 min protocol. Both ETFE 5 mL coils. Natural baseline reference candidate. Throughput 0.08 mmol/min.
uncertainties: Stage 2 ratio 0.83 is below batch; aminolysis completeness at 25 min unknown.
Equivalence between batch stirred and flow plug-flow exposure not established.
DPDTC solubility unconfirmed.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 sub-batch (τ1=25 min, ratio 0.83) in 2 mL PFA; Stage 2 extended (τ2=50 min, ratio 1.67) in ETFE 5 mL. Explores whether long aminolysis exposure compensates moderate Stage 1 hold. Lowest throughput group (0.04 mmol/min). Stream B at minimum pump flow 0.02 mL/min.
uncertainties: Stream B at 0.02 mL/min is at E-series minimum; pulsation risk.
Extended Stage 2 at 95 °C: amide or thioester degradation risk is untested hypothesis.
Stage 1 thioester completeness at 25 min unknown.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 extended (τ1=62.5 min, ratio 2.08) in ETFE 10 mL; Stage 2 near-batch (τ2=25 min, ratio 0.83). Tests highly extended thioester formation with moderate aminolysis. Total time 87.5 min. Throughput 0.08 mmol/min.
uncertainties: 62.5 min Stage 1 at 95 °C: DPDTC or thioester degradation is untested hypothesis.
Stage 2 at 25 min may not complete aminolysis; unknown.
Long total time conflicts with objective to avoid unnecessarily long residence times.

Conflicts with objective to avoid unnecessarily long residence times; warranted only as upper bound.

selection.objective_alignment: The objective requires maximising amide yield while avoiding unnecessarily long residence times. Candidate 4 anchors the screen at the batch reference condition without extending either stage beyond what the batch protocol demonstrated, satisfying both constraints simultaneously. It is the natural starting point for a balanced screen: shorter candidates (C1, C2, C3) test whether the batch times are unnecessarily long; longer candidates (C6, C7) test whether they are insufficient. Without kinetic data, C4 is the most defensible single selection for a first screen run because any yield gap relative to the batch result directly quantifies the flow penalty or equivalence, rather than conflating a time variable with a geometric variable.

alternatives.reason_not_selected: Stage 1 τ=35.7 min (1.19×) with Stage 2 τ=14.3 min (0.48×). Stage 2 is substantially below the batch anchor; with no kinetic data, incomplete amidation at 14.3 min is a plausible unresolved risk that makes this a higher-uncertainty candidate than C4 as the primary run. It is a scientifically valuable asymmetric contrast run after C4 results are in hand.

Stage 1 τ=16.7 min (0.56×) and Stage 2 τ=33.3 min (1.11×). Stage 1 is well below the batch anchor; incomplete thioester formation in Stage 1 propagates directly into Stage 2 and cannot be remedied by extended aminolysis time. PFA coil operates within 5 °C of its temperature limit, adding a thermostat-stability requirement. C2 is informative as an asymmetric contrast candidate once C4 establishes the baseline.

Stage 1 τ=62.5 min (2.08×) is more than double the batch anchor with an untested degradation risk for DPDTC and the thioester intermediate at 95 °C. Stage 2 at 25 min is also below batch. Total time 87.5 min conflicts with the objective to avoid unnecessarily long residence times unless shorter candidates show incomplete Stage 1 conversion.

literature_analogies: Analogy 1: SNAr condensation, Vapourtec R4+, 10 mL coil, 30 min, 0.5 M, 1.0 mL/min — similar: same residence time target and concentration; different: temperature 250 vs 95 °C and mechanism (SNAr vs NAS thioester); adjustment: temperature kept at batch-anchored 95 °C, flow rate reduced to 0.333 mL/min to maintain 30 min in 10 mL coil.

Analogy 2: dipolar cycloaddition CFU, 60 °C, 20 min, 0.165 mL/min — similar: two-reagent telescoped addition concept; different: lower temperature, different mechanism, no thioester; adjustment: not directly applicable for hardware parameters.

Analogy 3: condensation PFA coil 10 mL, 120 °C, 9.7 bar BPR — similar: above-boiling-point solvent operation with BPR, PFA coil, 10 mL reactor; different: higher temperature (120 vs 95 °C), different solvent; adjustment: BPR selected at 7 bar (lower than 9.7 bar) because 95 °C requires less suppression than 120 °C; PFA coil material directly adopted.
proposal.disposition_rationale: No deterministic hard-feasibility conflict was found. Treat the design as a first experimental screen until wet-lab evidence validates it.

Treat this proposal as a starting hypothesis requiring careful experimental validation before scale-up.

proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Chemistry Plan: benzylamine (Stream B) must not contact DPDTC before thioester formation is complete. Stage 1 effluent (thioester intermediate + residual DMAP + 2-pyridinethiol byproduct in 2-MeTHF) is mixed with Stream B at a T-mixer placed downstream of Reactor 1 and upstream of Reactor 2. A PEEK or ETFE T-mixer (P-713 or P-632) is used. This replicates the batch sequential addition (cool, open, add benzylamine, reseal, reheat) in a continuous connected process without a physical cooling step.
pre_reactor_steps: Prepare Stream A stock solution: dissolve 3-methyl-4-nitrobenzoic acid (1.0 equiv), DPDTC (1.05 equiv), and DMAP (0.1 equiv) in 2-MeTHF to give 0.5 M substrate concentration. No deoxygenation required — protocol run under ambient atmosphere (Chemistry Plan deoxygenation_required = false).

Prepare Stream B stock solution: dissolve benzylamine in 2-MeTHF to give 2.1 M. Keep separate from DPDTC-containing Stream A at all times (incompatible pair). Verify benzylamine solubility at 2.1 M in 2-MeTHF before use.

Prime tubing and verify steady-state flow before collecting product. Assign Stream A to BLUE peristaltic pump (Vapourtec E-series BLUE); assign Stream B to second BLUE peristaltic pump or syringe pump (Chemyx with appropriate syringe row) — never use RED pump tubing with 2-MeTHF.

Set BPR to 7 bar downstream of Reactor 2 to maintain 2-MeTHF liquid at 95 °C (bp 80 °C at 1 atm; 7 bar provides sufficient back-pressure margin; Analogy 3 used 9.7 bar BPR for similar above-bp-solvent operation at 120 °C).
Heat Reactor 1 (Stage 1 PFA 10 mL coil) and Reactor 2 (Stage 2 PFA 10 mL coil) to 95 °C before starting flow.
post_reactor_steps: Collect effluent from BPR outlet. No quench required between stages or at exit — Chemistry Plan quench_required = false.
Offline workup (extraction, purification) as described in batch protocol. Do not perform workup inline.
proposal.chemistry_notes: Two-stage telescoped thermal nucleophilic acyl substitution. Stage 1: 3-methyl-4-nitrobenzoic acid activated by DPDTC (DMAP-catalyzed) to form 2-pyridyl thioester intermediate at 95 °C, 30 min. Stage 2: benzylamine introduced at interstage T-mixer; thioester aminolysis at 95 °C, ~24 min (10 mL coil at 0.416 mL/min combined flow) as a screening start point — can be extended to ~36 min by adding one 5 mL PFA coil in series. No light required. BPR mandatory: 2-MeTHF bp 80 °C, reaction at 95 °C; 7 bar BPR selected from inventory. PFA coils required (max 100 °C); FEP coils excluded (max 50 °C). RED pump tubing excluded for 2-MeTHF; BLUE peristaltic or syringe pumps used for both streams. No deoxygenation. DPDTC/benzylamine incompatible pair strictly separated — Stream B introduced only after Stage 1 is complete. Concentration in Stage 2 reactor after mixing: substrate-derived species ~0.40 M (0.5 M × 0.333/0.416), benzylamine ~0.42 M (2.1 M × 0.083/0.416). CO2 potentially generated in Stage 1 (hypothesized mechanism step 3); BPR suppresses gas slug formation. Batch cooling step before benzylamine addition is a manual handling artifact — flow process eliminates it per chemist hypothesis Q-HYP-001.

stage_parameters.notes: V/Q = 10.0/0.333 = 30.0 min. Re = rho*v*d/mu ~ 10 (laminar). ΔP ~ 0.13 bar (well within 34 bar PFA limit and 10 bar pump limit).

Combined flow after T-mixer = 0.333 + 0.083 = 0.416 mL/min. V/Q = 10.0/0.416 = 24.0 min screening start. Optional: add one PFA 5 mL coil (coil_row4) in series for ~36 min total Stage 2 residence if needed. Inventory allows two coil_row4 units. Coil_row5 quantity=1 — if same 10 mL PFA coil needed for both stages, use coil_row5 for Stage 1 and two coil_row4 (5 mL each, series) for Stage 2 to give 10 mL total Stage 2 volume from available inventory.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Stage 1: batch protocol (protocol fact, timed_hold stage 1 = 30 min at 95 °C) sets screening residence time at 30 min. Analogy 1 (30 min at 250 °C, 10 mL, 1.0 mL/min for SNAr) and Analogy 3 (20 min at 120 °C, 10 mL, condensation) both use 10 mL reactors and 20–30 min; our reaction is at lower temperature (95 °C) so 30 min is appropriate starting point. Engineering calculation: V_R = 10 mL, Q = 0.333 mL/min → τ = 30 min, consistent with batch anchor. Stage 2: 24 min at combined flow 0.416 mL/min in 10 mL coil — below batch 30 min; flow process eliminates manual cooling step, so net thermal exposure is comparable.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_basis: Single-phase liquid system throughout. No gas feed. Basis: reactor_volume / total_liquid_flow per stage. Stage 1: 10 mL / 0.333 mL/min = 30 min. Stage 2: 10 mL / 0.416 mL/min = 24 min.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Protocol fact: 95 °C for both stages. No intensification mandated (kinetics uncharacterized, Q-HYP-001 states batch conditions are reference not fixed targets). Analogy 1 increased temperature dramatically (25→250 °C) for SNAr; not applicable here as our reaction already runs hot. Analogy 3 operated at 120 °C — our 95 °C is within PFA coil limit of 100 °C.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 2-MeTHF bp = 80 °C at 1 atm; operation at 95 °C requires back-pressure to prevent boiling. BPR required (T > bp). Chemistry Plan confidence_notes confirm BPR recommended. Analogy 3 used 9.7 bar BPR for similar above-bp operation at 120 °C. Available inventory: 7 bar fixed BPR (bpr_row6) selected as nearest available above minimum needed to suppress 2-MeTHF at 95 °C (Antoine estimate: ~1.5–2 bar absolute needed; 7 bar provides ample margin). Adjustable BPR up to 8 bar (bpr_row3) is alternative. 7 bar fixed selected for simplicity and reproducibility.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: PFA required: operation at 95 °C exceeds FEP max temperature of 50 °C (inventory: FEP coils max 100 °C listed — NOTE inventory coil_row6 FEP max_temperature_C = 50.0; FEP strictly excluded). ETFE coils (max 100 °C) are an alternative but PFA preferred for chemical compatibility with 2-MeTHF and halogenated/polar solvents. Chemistry Plan: 'PFA or ETFE (not FEP, max 50 °C)'. PFA 10 mL ID 1 mm (coil_row5) selected for Stage 1.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: Protocol fact: 0.5 M substrate in 2-MeTHF for Stage 1. Analogy 1 used 0.5 M — directly matches. Stream A prepared at 0.5 M substrate; DPDTC at 0.525 M and DMAP at 0.05 M in same solution. After Stage 2 mixing, substrate-derived species diluted to ~0.40 M (volume dilution by Stream B addition).
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Stream A: 0.333 mL/min gives τ = 30 min in 10 mL Stage 1 coil. Stream B: 0.083 mL/min gives 1.05 equiv benzylamine relative to substrate (2.1 M × 0.083 = 0.175 mmol/min; substrate 0.5 M × 0.333 = 0.167 mmol/min; ratio = 1.05). Analogy 1 used two streams at 0.5 mL/min each (1.0 mL/min total) for 10 mL reactor at 30 min — our lower flow is appropriate given same residence time target with only 1 feed stream in Stage 1. Engineering calculation: Q_total = V/τ = 10/30 = 0.333 mL/min. Re = ρvd/μ ≈ 10 (laminar, confirmed). Both flow rates within BLUE peristaltic pump range (0.02–10 mL/min).
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: Coil reactor — Chemistry Plan Stage 1 and Stage 2 both specify coil. Analogies 1 and 3 both use coil reactors. Plug flow confirmed: Pe = 691 (engineering calculation).
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID — all available PFA coils in inventory are 1.0 mm ID (coil_row3, row4, row5). Engineering calculation used 1.0 mm. Thermal: uniform heating confirmed for small ID. Pressure drop 0.13 bar (Step 5 calculation) well within pump limits.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: 10 mL PFA coil (coil_row5) for Stage 1: gives exactly 30 min at 0.333 mL/min. Stage 2: 10 mL total volume needed (from two coil_row4 5 mL PFA coils in series, or coil_row5 if available after Stage 1 assignment — inventory has 1× coil_row5 and 2× coil_row4; use coil_row5 for Stage 1 and 2× coil_row4 in series for Stage 2 to achieve 10 mL). Analogy 1 and Analogy 3 both used 10 mL reactors. Engineering calculation: V_R = 30 min × 0.333 mL/min = 10 mL (Stage 1).
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: No light required. Thermal nucleophilic acyl substitution — no photocatalyst, no chromophore. Chemistry Plan requires_light = false for both stages. wavelength_nm set to null.
reasoning_per_field.deoxygenation_method: None required. Protocol explicitly states ambient atmosphere without inert gas purging. Chemistry Plan deoxygenation_required = false.
reasoning_per_field.mixer_type: T-mixer at Stage 2 inlet to combine Stage 1 effluent with Stream B (benzylamine). P-632 ETFE T-mixer (quantity 22, available) or P-713 PEEK T-mixer selected. Chemistry Plan mixing_order_reasoning requires sequential addition with benzylamine only after thioester formation.

literature_analogies: Analogy 1: SNAr condensation, Vapourtec R4+, 10 mL coil, 30 min, 0.5 M, 1.0 mL/min — similar: same residence time target and concentration; different: temperature 250 vs 95 °C and mechanism (SNAr vs NAS thioester); adjustment: temperature kept at batch-anchored 95 °C, flow rate reduced to 0.333 mL/min to maintain 30 min in 10 mL coil.

Analogy 2: dipolar cycloaddition CFU, 60 °C, 20 min, 0.165 mL/min — similar: two-reagent telescoped addition concept; different: lower temperature, different mechanism, no thioester; adjustment: not directly applicable for hardware parameters.

Analogy 3: condensation PFA coil 10 mL, 120 °C, 9.7 bar BPR — similar: above-boiling-point solvent operation with BPR, PFA coil, 10 mL reactor; different: higher temperature (120 vs 95 °C), different solvent; adjustment: BPR selected at 7 bar (lower than 9.7 bar) because 95 °C requires less suppression than 120 °C; PFA coil material directly adopted.

literature_analogies: Analogy 1: SNAr condensation, Vapourtec R4+, 10 mL coil, 30 min, 0.5 M, 1.0 mL/min — similar: same residence time target and concentration; different: temperature 250 vs 95 °C and mechanism (SNAr vs NAS thioester); adjustment: temperature kept at batch-anchored 95 °C, flow rate reduced to 0.333 mL/min to maintain 30 min in 10 mL coil.

Analogy 2: dipolar cycloaddition CFU, 60 °C, 20 min, 0.165 mL/min — similar: two-reagent telescoped addition concept; different: lower temperature, different mechanism, no thioester; adjustment: not directly applicable for hardware parameters.

Analogy 3: condensation PFA coil 10 mL, 120 °C, 9.7 bar BPR — similar: above-boiling-point solvent operation with BPR, PFA coil, 10 mL reactor; different: higher temperature (120 vs 95 °C), different solvent; adjustment: BPR selected at 7 bar (lower than 9.7 bar) because 95 °C requires less suppression than 120 °C; PFA coil material directly adopted.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates.

computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates.

computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

Adequate as a sub-batch baseline screening point; Stage 1 thioester formation and Stage 2 aminolysis may both be incomplete at these holds.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates.

computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

DrChemistry.justification: Both stages below batch anchor (τ1=17.9 min, τ2=14.3 min; ratios 0.60/0.48). Provides the shortest-time exploratory point. Uses two ETFE 5 mL coils at highest throughput (0.14 mmol/min). Adequate as a sub-batch baseline screening point; Stage 1 thioester formation and Stage 2 aminolysis may both be incomplete at these holds.
uncertainties: Stage 1 thioester conversion unknown at 17.9 min; sub-batch hold may leave unreacted acid.
Stage 2 aminolysis at 14.3 min may be insufficient; untested.

selection.objective_alignment: The objective requires maximising amide yield while avoiding unnecessarily long residence times. Candidate 4 anchors the screen at the batch reference condition without extending either stage beyond what the batch protocol demonstrated, satisfying both constraints simultaneously. It is the natural starting point for a balanced screen: shorter candidates (C1, C2, C3) test whether the batch times are unnecessarily long; longer candidates (C6, C7) test whether they are insufficient. Without kinetic data, C4 is the most defensible single selection for a first screen run because any yield gap relative to the batch result directly quantifies the flow penalty or equivalence, rather than conflating a time variable with a geometric variable.

alternatives.reason_not_selected: Stage 1 τ=35.7 min (1.19×) with Stage 2 τ=14.3 min (0.48×). Stage 2 is substantially below the batch anchor; with no kinetic data, incomplete amidation at 14.3 min is a plausible unresolved risk that makes this a higher-uncertainty candidate than C4 as the primary run. It is a scientifically valuable asymmetric contrast run after C4 results are in hand.

Stage 1 τ=16.7 min (0.56×) and Stage 2 τ=33.3 min (1.11×). Stage 1 is well below the batch anchor; incomplete thioester formation in Stage 1 propagates directly into Stage 2 and cannot be remedied by extended aminolysis time. PFA coil operates within 5 °C of its temperature limit, adding a thermostat-stability requirement. C2 is informative as an asymmetric contrast candidate once C4 establishes the baseline.

Stage 1 τ=62.5 min (2.08×) is more than double the batch anchor with an untested degradation risk for DPDTC and the thioester intermediate at 95 °C. Stage 2 at 25 min is also below batch. Total time 87.5 min conflicts with the objective to avoid unnecessarily long residence times unless shorter candidates show incomplete Stage 1 conversion.

literature_analogies: Analogy 1: SNAr condensation, Vapourtec R4+, 10 mL coil, 30 min, 0.5 M, 1.0 mL/min — similar: same residence time target and concentration; different: temperature 250 vs 95 °C and mechanism (SNAr vs NAS thioester); adjustment: temperature kept at batch-anchored 95 °C, flow rate reduced to 0.333 mL/min to maintain 30 min in 10 mL coil.

Analogy 2: dipolar cycloaddition CFU, 60 °C, 20 min, 0.165 mL/min — similar: two-reagent telescoped addition concept; different: lower temperature, different mechanism, no thioester; adjustment: not directly applicable for hardware parameters.

Analogy 3: condensation PFA coil 10 mL, 120 °C, 9.7 bar BPR — similar: above-boiling-point solvent operation with BPR, PFA coil, 10 mL reactor; different: higher temperature (120 vs 95 °C), different solvent; adjustment: BPR selected at 7 bar (lower than 9.7 bar) because 95 °C requires less suppression than 120 °C; PFA coil material directly adopted.

mechanism_steps.description: Hypothesis: DMAP attacks DPDTC to form a DMAP-activated carbonate intermediate, releasing 2-pyridinethiol.
Hypothesis: The carboxylate oxygen of 3-methyl-4-nitrobenzoic acid attacks the DMAP-activated intermediate to form a mixed anhydride/activated ester, regenerating DMAP. CO2 may be released.

Benzylamine attacks the thioester carbonyl carbon (aminolysis), forming a tetrahedral intermediate.

chemistry_plan.mixing_order_reasoning: Stream A components (carboxylic acid + DPDTC + DMAP) must be combined and heated first to form the thioester intermediate (Stage 1). Benzylamine (Stream B) must NOT contact DPDTC before thioester formation is complete, as the amine could react directly with DPDTC, forming an undesired carbamate or consuming the coupling reagent. Therefore, Stream B is introduced only at the Stage 2 T-mixer after Stage 1 residence is complete. The batch protocol explicitly cools, opens, adds benzylamine, then reheats — in flow, this sequential addition is achieved by the two-stage reactor topology.
chemistry_plan.deoxygenation_reasoning: The batch protocol explicitly states 'under ambient atmosphere without argon or nitrogen purging.' No oxygen-sensitive species are present.
chemistry_plan.quench_reasoning: No quench is described between stages in the batch protocol. The batch protocol proceeds directly to workup after Stage 2. Any workup (extraction, etc.) would be done offline after collection.
chemistry_plan.confidence_notes: DPDTC structure: assumed to be di(2-pyridyl) dithiocarbonate based on MW ~248 matching 130 mg / 0.525 mmol; the exact SMILES for DPDTC may involve thio-carbonate linkages (S instead of O) — the provided SMILES uses oxygen and may need correction. The mechanism steps (1–3) for thioester formation are hypothesized based on analogy to DCC/DMAP chemistry and may differ for DPDTC specifically. The rate-limiting step is unknown — both stages use 30 min in batch but no conversion-vs-time data exists. The 2.1 M benzylamine concentration in Stream B assumes solubility in 2-MeTHF at room temperature, which should be verified. The system must operate above atmospheric pressure (BPR recommended, e.g., 2.5 or 7 bar) to keep 2-MeTHF liquid at 95 °C (bp 80 °C). CO2 generation during thioester formation is a hypothesis and could cause gas slugs in Stage 1 — a BPR would help suppress this. Reactor volume selection: Stage 1 uses 10 mL PFA coil at ~0.33 mL/min for 30 min residence; Stage 2 uses a second coil with combined flow ~0.42 mL/min. These are starting-point estimates.

batch_record.raw_text: A 4.0 mL vial equipped with a PTFE stir bar was charged with 3-methyl-4-nitrobenzoic acid (1 equiv, 0.5 mmol), N,N-dimethylpyridin-4-amine (DMAP) (6.1 mg, 0.1 equiv, 0.05 mmol), and DPDTC (130. mg, 1.05 equiv, 0.525 mmol) under ambient atmosphere without argon or nitrogen purging.  2-MeTHF (1.0 mL, 0.5 M) was added, and the vial was capped and sealed with Teflon tape. The reaction vial was placed in a pre-heated oil bath maintained at 95 °C and stirred at 500–600 rpm for 30 min. The vial was removed from the oil bath and allowed to cool at room temperature for 5–10 min. Once cooled, the cap was removed and benzylamine (1.05 equiv, 0.525 mmol) and 2-MeTHF (0.25 mL, 0.4 M) were quickly added. The vial was capped, sealed with Teflon tape, and returned to the oil bath at 95 °C, and stirred at 500–600 rpm for another 30 min before workup.

intake_package.raw_protocol: A 4.0 mL vial equipped with a PTFE stir bar was charged with 3-methyl-4-nitrobenzoic acid (1 equiv, 0.5 mmol), N,N-dimethylpyridin-4-amine (DMAP) (6.1 mg, 0.1 equiv, 0.05 mmol), and DPDTC (130. mg, 1.05 equiv, 0.525 mmol) under ambient atmosphere without argon or nitrogen purging.  2-MeTHF (1.0 mL, 0.5 M) was added, and the vial was capped and sealed with Teflon tape. The reaction vial was placed in a pre-heated oil bath maintained at 95 °C and stirred at 500–600 rpm for 30 min. The vial was removed from the oil bath and allowed to cool at room temperature for 5–10 min. Once cooled, the cap was removed and benzylamine (1.05 equiv, 0.525 mmol) and 2-MeTHF (0.25 mL, 0.4 M) were quickly added. The vial was capped, sealed with Teflon tape, and returned to the oil bath at 95 °C, and stirred at 500–600 rpm for another 30 min before workup.

hypotheses: Stage 1 conversion will directly affect the amount of thioester available for Stage 2 amidation. The cooling step before benzylamine addition may be a batch-handling step rather than an essential reaction step and should be evaluated in flow. Use the batch temperature and reaction times as reference conditions rather than fixed targets, and determine the operating conditions based on flow performance. The Stream A/Stream B molar ratio should match the intended stoichiometry, taking both concentration and flow rate into account.

operating_limits.equipment_assembly_policy: Mount tubing only in its declared compatible module, respecting module capacity, temperature and shared quantity. UV-150 lights are not detachable: use UV-150 with an E-series or R-series platform; external syringe cofeeds are permitted when necessary. Manual modules use their own strip lights.
operating_limits.pump_platform_policy: Prefer compatible channels within one system. Mixed platforms are permitted but disfavored; justify necessity, especially reagent incompatibility requiring an external syringe pump. Do not force every UV-150 feed onto system pumps.
operating_limits.reporting: Report each feed component concentration, molar flow and equivalent; distinguish theoretical intermediate concentration. Report gas volume at inlet STP in mL/min.

operating_limits.pump_setting_policy: Minimum flow is the lower operating limit. Adjustment flow is the setting increment, represented as multiples of that increment; jointly solve all feeds without changing stated stoichiometry.

chemistry_identity_confirmation.chemist_description: This is a two-stage DPDTC-mediated amide formation through a thioester intermediate. In Stage 1, 3-methyl-4-nitrobenzoic acid is converted to the corresponding 2-pyridyl thioester using DPDTC and DMAP, without isolating the intermediate. In Stage 2, benzylamine is added to the Stage 1 effluent to form N-benzyl-3-methyl-4-nitrobenzamide. The amide C(O)–N bond is formed and the thioester C(O)–S bond is cleaved during Stage 2.

answers.answer: Develop a safe, reproducible, and inventory-compatible two-stage telescoped flow process that maximizes the final amide yield while avoiding unnecessarily long residence times. Design the two stages as one connected process, because Stage 1 determines the composition entering Stage 2.

This is a two-stage DPDTC-mediated amide formation through a thioester intermediate. In Stage 1, 3-methyl-4-nitrobenzoic acid is converted to the corresponding 2-pyridyl thioester using DPDTC and DMAP, without isolating the intermediate. In Stage 2, benzylamine is added to the Stage 1 effluent to form N-benzyl-3-methyl-4-nitrobenzamide. The amide C(O)–N bond is formed and the thioester C(O)–S bond is cleaved during Stage 2.

Stage 1 conversion will directly affect the amount of thioester available for Stage 2 amidation. The cooling step before benzylamine addition may be a batch-handling step rather than an essential reaction step and should be evaluated in flow. Use the batch temperature and reaction times as reference conditions rather than fixed targets, and determine the operating conditions based on flow performance. The Stream A/Stream B molar ratio should match the intended stoichiometry, taking both concentration and flow rate into account.

answer.equipment_assembly_policy: Mount tubing only in its declared compatible module, respecting module capacity, temperature and shared quantity. UV-150 lights are not detachable: use UV-150 with an E-series or R-series platform; external syringe cofeeds are permitted when necessary. Manual modules use their own strip lights.
answer.pump_platform_policy: Prefer compatible channels within one system. Mixed platforms are permitted but disfavored; justify necessity, especially reagent incompatibility requiring an external syringe pump. Do not force every UV-150 feed onto system pumps.
answer.reporting: Report each feed component concentration, molar flow and equivalent; distinguish theoretical intermediate concentration. Report gas volume at inlet STP in mL/min.
catalog_projection_limits: Fabricatable tubing remains stock, not installed reactor candidates; strict < versus up-to volume needs confirmation.
Red/green strip wavelengths unspecified: retained in source catalog, not wavelength-selectable candidates.
Integrated H-Cube retained in source catalog, not decomposed into external pump/MFC/BPR.
Unknown check-valve pressure rating and MFC quantity require laboratory verification.
Compatibility PDF is not a certification for unlisted solutes or mixtures.
answer.pump_setting_policy: Minimum flow is the lower operating limit. Adjustment flow is the setting increment, represented as multiples of that increment; jointly solve all feeds without changing stated stoichiometry.

proposal.residence_time_basis: sum of per-stage liquid-only reactor-volume times

streams.pump_role: Stage 1 feed — delivers substrate, coupling reagent, and catalyst to Reactor 1
streams.reasoning: Deterministic stoichiometric flow solution: Q_A=k*(equiv/C)=0.28 mL/min; equiv=1, C=0.5 M; pump=pump_e_series_blue; concentration_basis=reference component: 3-methyl-4-nitrobenzoic acid; equiv_basis=reference component: 3-methyl-4-nitrobenzoic acid.

streams.pump_role: Stage 2 cofeed — delivers benzylamine nucleophile at the interstage T-mixer
contents: benzylamine (1.05 equiv relative to substrate, neat or concentrated in 2-MeTHF)
streams.reasoning: Deterministic stoichiometric flow solution: Q_B=k*(equiv/C)=0.07 mL/min; equiv=1.05, C=2.1 M; pump=pump_e_series_blue; concentration_basis=chemistry_plan; equiv_basis=protocol_fact.

proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Chemistry Plan: benzylamine (Stream B) must not contact DPDTC before thioester formation is complete. Stage 1 effluent (thioester intermediate + residual DMAP + 2-pyridinethiol byproduct in 2-MeTHF) is mixed with Stream B at a T-mixer placed downstream of Reactor 1 and upstream of Reactor 2. A PEEK or ETFE T-mixer (P-713 or P-632) is used. This replicates the batch sequential addition (cool, open, add benzylamine, reseal, reheat) in a continuous connected process without a physical cooling step.
pre_reactor_steps: Prepare Stream A containing 3-methyl-4-nitrobenzoic acid (1.0 equiv, 0.5 M), DPDTC (1.05 equiv, 0.525 M), DMAP (0.1 equiv, 0.05 M), 2-MeTHF (2-methyltetrahydrofuran) in 2-MeTHF (2-methyltetrahydrofuran) at 0.5 M; concentration basis: reference component: 3-methyl-4-nitrobenzoic acid.
Prepare Stream B containing benzylamine (1.05 equiv relative to substrate, neat or concentrated in 2-MeTHF) in 2-MeTHF (2-methyltetrahydrofuran) at 2.1 M; concentration basis: chemistry_plan.
Install Stage 1 reactor coil_row11 (5 mL, 2.4 mm ID, ETFE) at 95 deg C.
Install Stage 2 reactor coil_row11 (5 mL, 2.4 mm ID, ETFE) at 95 deg C.
Install assigned feeds A:pump_e_series_blue, B:pump_e_series_blue.
Set the outlet BPR to 7 bar gauge and start liquid feeds at final outlet flow 0.35 mL/min.

proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Chemistry Plan: benzylamine (Stream B) must not contact DPDTC before thioester formation is complete. Stage 1 effluent (thioester intermediate + residual DMAP + 2-pyridinethiol byproduct in 2-MeTHF) is mixed with Stream B at a T-mixer placed downstream of Reactor 1 and upstream of Reactor 2. A PEEK or ETFE T-mixer (P-713 or P-632) is used. This replicates the batch sequential addition (cool, open, add benzylamine, reseal, reheat) in a continuous connected process without a physical cooling step.
pre_reactor_steps: Prepare Stream A containing 3-methyl-4-nitrobenzoic acid (1.0 equiv, 0.5 M), DPDTC (1.05 equiv, 0.525 M), DMAP (0.1 equiv, 0.05 M), 2-MeTHF (2-methyltetrahydrofuran) in 2-MeTHF (2-methyltetrahydrofuran) at 0.5 M; concentration basis: reference component: 3-methyl-4-nitrobenzoic acid.
Prepare Stream B containing benzylamine (1.05 equiv relative to substrate, neat or concentrated in 2-MeTHF) in 2-MeTHF (2-methyltetrahydrofuran) at 2.1 M; concentration basis: chemistry_plan.
Install Stage 1 reactor coil_row12 (10 mL, 2.4 mm ID, ETFE) at 95 deg C.
Install Stage 2 reactor coil_row11 (5 mL, 2.4 mm ID, ETFE) at 95 deg C.
Install assigned feeds A:pump_e_series_blue, B:pump_e_series_blue.
Set the outlet BPR to 7 bar gauge and start liquid feeds at final outlet flow 0.2 mL/min.
post_reactor_steps: Collect effluent from BPR outlet. No quench required between stages or at exit — Chemistry Plan quench_required = false.
Collect only after the canonical residence-time stabilization period; use the inventory-compiled downstream path.
Collect only after the canonical residence-time stabilization period; use the inventory-compiled downstream path.
For shutdown, stop reactive cofeeds and reagent gas first, flush with a compatible declared solvent, then depressurize through the controlled outlet.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates.

computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates.

computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

common_issues: All candidates assign both Stream A and Stream B to 'pump_e_series_blue' as a single equipment_id, but two independent peristaltic channels are physically required. Laboratory must confirm two separate BLUE pump tubing channels are allocated before any candidate is executed.

No candidate explicitly assigns a T-mixer or Y-mixer for Stream B introduction at Stage 2. A union fitting is not a three-port mixer. Mixer selection must be confirmed from available inventory (P-632, P-713, P-513) before execution.
2-MeTHF is listed in excluded_chemicals for all RED pump tubing. All candidates correctly route 2-MeTHF through BLUE pump tubing; this is consistent and not a violation.

PFA coils (coil_row3, coil_row4) have max_temperature_C of 100 °C; operating at 95 °C leaves only 5 °C margin. Thermostat stability at this margin requires laboratory verification for candidates 2, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11.
Benzylamine Stream B concentration of 2.1 M in 2-MeTHF is not confirmed as a soluble, stable, homogeneous solution; laboratory must verify before use.
DPDTC solubility at 0.525 M in 2-MeTHF at the operating temperature is unconfirmed across all candidates.
All achieved stage hold ratios are V/Q liquid indices, not proven measures of chemical exposure equivalence to batch; kinetics are entirely uncharacterized.
No BPR_available list items are present in the hard constraints; BPR assignments (7 bar) use bpr_row6 (fixed, 1 unit available). Laboratory must confirm this unit is unallocated.

Candidates 11 and 12 carry label mismatches: target stage times of 120/30 and 120/120 min respectively are not achieved; actual holds are 62.5/20 and 62.5/50 min. These are not hard violations but must be corrected in experimental records to avoid confusion.

Extended Stage 1 and/or Stage 2 holds at 95 °C introduce a plausible but entirely untested degradation risk for DPDTC, the thioester intermediate, and the amide product. This is a hypothesis, not an established constraint, and does not veto any candidate.
No gas stages, photochemistry, or analogy kinetic data are applicable to this chemistry. No yield, conversion, or residence-time superiority can be claimed for any candidate.

selection.objective_alignment: The objective requires maximising amide yield while avoiding unnecessarily long residence times. _analogies.summary: This record describes a condensation reaction proceeding via nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) mechanism using DIPEA as base in DMA solvent. The reaction was performed in a Vapourtec R4+ flow reactor with a 10 mL reactor volume at 250°C with a 30-minute residence time and 1.0 mL/min flow rate, achieving 69% yield at 0.5 M concentration. The batch baseline was conducted at room temperature (25°C) for 30 minutes and achieved the same 69% yield. Flow chemistry enabled the use of significantly higher reaction temperature (250°C vs 25°C) while maintaining the same residence time and yield, suggesting improved reaction kinetics and process intensification through better heat transfer control in the continuous flow system.

chemistry.scope_summary: The synthesis involves condensation of 2-fluorobenzaldehydes with methylhydrazine to produce substituted indazoles. The reaction conditions were optimized for a range of electron-withdrawing and electron-donating groups. The methodology allows for rapid synthesis and scalability, suitable for generating a range of indazole analogues.

_analogies.summary: This process demonstrates a [3 + 2] dipolar cycloaddition reaction conducted in a continuous flow unit (CFU) with automated pumps. The reaction uses DMSO as solvent with diisopropylamine as base, operating at 60°C with a 20-minute residence time at 0.165 mL/min flow rate, achieving 96% yield. The flow process allows for higher temperature operation (60°C vs 20°C in batch) while maintaining excellent yield, with the batch baseline achieving 100% yield at room temperature in the same reaction time. The continuous flow setup enables better temperature control and process intensification, allowing the reaction to proceed efficiently at elevated temperature with only a minimal decrease in yield compared to the batch process.

_analogies.summary: This condensation reaction was conducted as a thermal process using piperidine as a base in a 1:1 DMSO:water solvent mixture at 120°C. The flow system employed a PFA tubing reactor with a 10 mL volume, Milligat pumps, and a 9.7 bar back-pressure regulator to maintain reaction conditions. The reaction time was significantly reduced from 1.33 hours in batch to just 20 minutes residence time in flow, representing a 4-fold intensification factor. Both batch and flow processes achieved the same 43% yield, but flow provided substantial time savings while maintaining equivalent performance. The flow setup enabled precise temperature and pressure control through the back-pressure regulator, allowing for efficient processing at the elevated temperature required for this condensation reaction.
